Rewiring Cost Malaysia (2026): Electrical Wiring Quotation Guide

Published 27 November 2026

Rewiring a home in Malaysia costs roughly RM3,000–12,000 for a 2–3 bedroom condo, RM5,000–15,000 for a single-storey terrace and RM8,000–20,000 for a double-storey terrace in 2026, according to published price guides. Individual points run at about RM95–150 for a 13A socket and RM95–140 for a lighting point, and a new single-phase DB box adds about RM1,500–3,500. A good electrical wiring quotation prices each of these as a separate line, so the client sees what they are paying for.

Rewiring cost in Malaysia by home type (2026)

A full rewire means new cables, sockets, switches and lighting points throughout, usually with a new distribution board (DB box). Published ranges differ by source, so here they are side by side:

Home type ClickBina (2026) wiringrumah.my (Jul 2026)
Studio or small apartment (under 700 sq ft) RM4,000–8,000 –
Apartment or 2–3 bedroom condo RM6,000–12,000 RM3,000–6,000
Single-storey terrace RM8,000–15,000 RM5,000–10,000
Double-storey terrace RM12,000–20,000 RM8,000–15,000
Semi-D or bungalow RM15,000–30,000+ RM12,000–25,000+

A partial rewire, such as one section, the kitchen or added points in the living areas, costs about RM1,000–5,000 in both wiringrumah.my’s and iHome.my’s 2026 figures. iHome.my puts a full rewire at RM4,000–15,000 for a whole house, and the itemised costs PropertyGuru cites from iDFAC Engineering put it at RM3,500–10,000+ per project.

What moves the price:

  • Number of points. reno.my estimates about 35–50 points for a three-bedroom flat and 60–90 points for a full rewire of a double-storey terrace.
  • Concealed or surface wiring. ClickBina prices a socket on surface trunking near the DB at RM120–250, but a concealed (chased-in) socket at RM200–400, because the wall has to be cut and patched.
  • Cable run length. A socket on a long run far from the board costs RM350–600 in ClickBina’s figures.
  • DB box. Replacing the board is often the single biggest line (see below).

Wiring price per point

Most electricians in Malaysia quote by the point: one socket, one lighting point or one appliance point, with the cable from the board included. Here are the 2026 rates by source:

Point Published rate Source
13A socket point (cable and back box included) RM95–130 reno.my (Aug 2026)
13A socket point RM100–150 Qanvast (Dec 2025); iDFAC via PropertyGuru
Lighting point with switch (fitting not included) RM95–140 reno.my
Ceiling lighting point RM65–100 Qanvast
Electrical point RM65–90 iDFAC via PropertyGuru
Recessed LED downlight, supply & install RM60–150 ClickBina
Aircon point (dedicated RCD) RM180–280 reno.my
15A socket point RM200–250 Qanvast
20A socket point RM250–280 Qanvast
Water heater point (heavier cable, isolator) RM200–300 reno.my
Dedicated appliance circuit with new breaker from RM400 ClickBina

Weatherproof outdoor point RM250–500 ClickBina

Some electricians price labour only, with the client or main contractor supplying materials. wiringrumah.my lists starting labour prices of RM80 per plug point, RM60 per light or downlight, RM150 per fan and RM300 per water heater. If you quote this way, say clearly in the quotation that cable, sockets and fittings are excluded.

DB box, RCCB and MCB costs

The DB box (distribution board, also called the consumer unit) holds the main switch, the RCCB that trips on earth leakage, and the MCBs that protect each circuit. ClickBina’s 2026 Klang Valley ranges:

Item Published rate
Add or replace a single RCCB, MCB or RCBO RM250–600
Standard single-phase consumer unit upgrade RM1,500–3,500
Split-load board with two RCCBs RM2,000–4,000
Three-phase board RM3,500–8,000+
Fault-finding or tripping diagnosis RM150–400
Electrical inspection with test report, condo or small unit RM150–400
Electrical inspection with test report, landed house RM400–900

reno.my lists a new distribution board with MCBs and an RCD as part of a full rewire, along with insulation testing and a completion certificate. If your price includes the board, name it on its own line. If it doesn’t, write that the existing board is retained.

Who can do the wiring

Electrical work is regulated by the Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga), not by CIDB alone. The Commission says contractors and wiremen must hold a valid licence it has issued before carrying out electrical installation work. Under the Electricity Regulations 1994, as published by the Commission:

  • Regulation 75: electrical work may only be carried out by a holder of a valid Certificate of Registration as an Electrical Contractor.
  • Regulation 12: wiring on a single-phase supply must be under the immediate supervision of a qualified wireman, employed full-time by the electrical contractor, who certifies a Supervision and Completion Certificate when the work is finished.
  • Regulations 13 and 14: the installation must then be tested by an authorised wireman, who certifies a Test Certificate. These are Forms G and H.

For a renovation contractor, this usually means subcontracting the electrical package to a registered electrical contractor, or holding that registration yourself, and handing the client the certificates at completion. You can check a contractor on the Energy Commission’s list of registered electrical contractors. CIDB also has a separate specialisation code for wiring (E04); see the CIDB registration guide.

This is general information, not legal advice. Check the current rules with the Energy Commission.

Sample electrical wiring quotation (illustrative)

This is an illustrative quotation for a full rewire of a three-bedroom condo with 39 points, inside reno.my’s 35–50 range. Every rate sits inside the published ranges above. Use your own rates.

Item Unit Qty Rate (RM) Amount (RM)
Lighting point with switch, cable included (fitting excluded) point 16 110.00 1,760.00
13A socket point, cable and back box included point 18 120.00 2,160.00
Aircon point with dedicated RCD point 3 230.00 690.00
Water heater point with isolator point 2 250.00 500.00
Single-phase consumer unit (DB box) upgrade, with RCCB and MCBs lot 1 2,200.00 2,200.00
Inspection and test report lot 1 300.00 300.00
Total 7,610.00

Excluded: light fittings, ceiling fans, aircon units and water heaters; wall patching and repainting after chasing; TNB applications for a supply upgrade; and management deposits. The total works out to about RM195 per point across the 39 points, and sits inside ClickBina’s RM6,000–12,000 range for a 2–3 bedroom condo.

What to put in an electrical wiring quotation

  • A point schedule by room. reno.my’s per-room estimates are a useful check: about 8–12 points in the living room, 10–14 in the kitchen, 6–9 per bedroom, 2–4 per bathroom and 4–8 for the exterior and staircase.
  • The type of each point. Separate 13A sockets, lighting points, and aircon and water heater points, because the rates differ.
  • Cable and wiring method. reno.my suggests stating the cable type. Say whether the wiring is concealed or in surface trunking.
  • The DB box. New or retained, single- or three-phase, and how many RCCBs.
  • Testing and certification. Name the test report and the certificates you will hand over.
  • Making good. Who patches and paints the chased walls. wiringrumah.my lists drilling and wall finishing among the items a full quotation should cover.

If the client adds points after the walls are closed, price them with a variation order before the work starts. Commercial jobs may also attract service tax if you are registered; see the SST guide.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to rewire a house in Malaysia in 2026?
Published 2026 guides put a full rewire of a 2–3 bedroom condo at roughly RM3,000 to RM12,000, a single-storey terrace at RM5,000 to RM15,000, a double-storey terrace at RM8,000 to RM20,000, and a semi-D or bungalow from RM12,000 to RM30,000 or more. The number of points, the cable runs and whether the DB box is replaced decide where a job lands.
How much is wiring per point in Malaysia?
2026 price guides put a 13A socket point at roughly RM95 to RM150 and a lighting point with switch at roughly RM95 to RM140, with cable and back box included. Aircon and water heater points cost more, at about RM180 to RM300, because they need heavier cable and an isolator or their own circuit.
How much does it cost to change a DB box in Malaysia?
One Klang Valley contractor guide puts a standard single-phase consumer unit (DB box) upgrade at RM1,500 to RM3,500, a split-load board with two RCCBs at RM2,000 to RM4,000, and a three-phase board from RM3,500 to RM8,000 or more. Adding or replacing a single RCCB, MCB or RCBO costs about RM250 to RM600.
Who is allowed to do electrical wiring in Malaysia?
The Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga) requires contractors and wiremen to hold a valid licence before carrying out electrical installation work. Under the Electricity Regulations 1994, electrical work is done by a registered Electrical Contractor, and a qualified wireman supervises, tests and certifies the installation.
How many electrical points does a house have?
One 2026 guide puts a full rewire of a three-bedroom flat at about 35 to 50 points and a double-storey terrace at about 60 to 90 points. Counting the points room by room is the most reliable way to build an electrical quotation.
